mechanism_narrative: MET (RTK) and LIFR (cytokine receptor) are co-expressed in aged MuSC, MF-I, and MF-II cells with MET showing modest expression (pc~0.15-0.23) and LIFR showing strong expression (pc~0.16-0.34) that declines with age. The flexible_GS4 linker (~20A) forces close proximity between MET's kinase domain (residues 1078-1345) and LIFR's JAK-associated intracellular region (no intrinsic kinase). Under forced co-clustering, MET's kinase transphosphorylates LIFR's JAK-docking tyrosines, creating hybrid phospho-sites that recruit GRB2/SHC1 (MAPK), GAB1/PIK3R1 (PI3K/AKT), and STAT3 - a biased output that excludes PLCg (sterically blocked by the tight ~20A spacing) and FRS2 (which requires FGFR-specific juxtamembrane docking absent in both receptors). The resulting MAPK/AKT/STAT3 signaling drives a muscle structural gene program (ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11, TAGLN) while suppressing aged IEG markers (EGR1, FOS, JUN, IL32, TXNIP), producing a transcriptional shift toward the young muscle phenotype.
